text:
maria: Quick heads-up — sandbox shows an org key routing into a project GPU pool even though no X-Project header was sent.

josh: Paste the curl?

maria: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer org_pk_ABC" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gptx-8k","prompt":"hi"}'
(no X-Project header, still lands in project-prod pool in console)

kevin: That matches legacy sticky-affinity — we bind an org key to the last-used project for 5m to reduce cold starts.

sophia: Any auth-router decision trace? Which code path set the pool?

maria: auth-router log: decision=sticky_affinity pool=project-prod ttl_seconds=300

josh: The problem: billing is inconsistent. Some calls meter against org quota, others against project quota. Support tickets spiking.

kevin: Routing (pool selection) and metering (attribution) are currently decoupled. If they diverge during request lifetime attribution can flip.

sophia: Proposed fixes: (1) deterministic attribution precedence: X-Project header -> impersonation claim -> sticky affinity fallback; (2) emit telemetry event when route_owner != meter_owner; (3) sample full request traces for investigation.

ops-oncall: Please enable 1:100 sampled full traces (headers + route decision + meter decision) for 24h in sandbox.

maria: Added sampling flag authz.trace=sticky-mismatch and query on request_trace for mismatches. Filed OBS-8001 and assigned to maria, kevin.

kevin: Canary plan: (A) set sticky_affinity_ttl=0 in sandbox behind a feature-flag, (B) monitor mismatch telemetry, (C) run unit/integration tests for attribution precedence, (D) consider an opt-out header like X-Routing-Prefer=pool for customers that want explicit binding.

sophia: UX ask: console request detail should surface "effective auth" (e.g. "org_key (sticky->project-prod)") so support can triage without digging traces.

maria: Will attach sample traces to OBS-8001 and monitor. If sandbox is clean after 2h we can promote to staging. Thanks all :thumbsup:
